claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor intrinsic oxygen resistance and undergoes rapid oxidation with substantial oxygen ingress at high temperature.
A Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating can be deposited by a fused-slurry process followed by high-temperature treatment.
Applying that coating process to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will produce a dual-layer silicide structure.
The coating will contain a high-silicon outer layer and a lower-silicon inner silicide layer.
The high-silicon outer layer will oxidize to form a dense, adherent film containing SiO2 and Cr-rich oxides.
The inner silicide layer will remain bonded to the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
The coating-derived oxide and silicide layers will act as barriers to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will be chemically inert with respect to the alloy's bulk BCC matrix.
Because the coating is thin and chemically inert, it will not compromise the dislocation mechanisms responsible for the alloy's ductility and strength.
The coating will significantly reduce oxide-scale growth and oxidation mass gain relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve the room-temperature tensile ductility of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve the elevated-temperature yield strength and creep performance of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will remain effective during static-air exposure at 800–1000 °C for approximately 50–100 h.
The coated alloy will retain useful performance under room-temperature and elevated-temperature mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Long-term coating stability under thermal cycling and possible coating–substrate interfacial reactions are unresolved.
